texts.preamble: Joshi vs The State Food Insepctor on 11 January, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Monday, The 11Th Day Of January 2016/21St Pousha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 674 of 2008 ( ) -------------------------------- Crl.A 830/2006 of Addl.District And Sessions Court (Adhoc)-Ii, Kozhikode Cc 300/2005 of Spl.J.M.F.C. For Trial Of Maradu Cases, Kozhikode Revision Petitioner/Appellant/Accused:: ---------------------------------------------------------------- Joshi, S/O. Sahadevan, (Blue Land, Neerkunnam P.O., Alappuzha) Now Residing At Patteeri House, Near Veteniary Hospital, Kozhikode-1. By Adv. Sri.Pradeesh Chacko Respondents/Respondents/Complainant & State:: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1. The State Food Insepctor, Kozhikode Corporation. 2. The State Of Kerala, Represented By Public Prosecutor High Court Of Kerala, Ernakulam. R1 & R2 By Public Prosecutor, Shri.R.Githesh This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 11-01-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: B.Sudheendra Kumar, J. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - -- - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - Joshi vs The State Food Insepctor on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193811281/ 1 Crl.R.P. No.674 of 2008 - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - Dated this the 11th day of January 2016 O R D E R
texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 7.1.2004 at about 1.20 p.m.,, PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 2 plates of vegetable biriyani from the shop of the first accused. After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P12 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for Biriyani under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1956 and therefore, the same was adulterated. It was further reported that the sample contained synthetic colour. Thereafter, on the request of the accused, second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext .P13 report of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample contained synthetic colour tartarsin and sunset yellow and therefore, it was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts. P1 to P23 were marked for the prosecution. DW1 was examined and Exts.D1 and D2 were marked for the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P13 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P13 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Joshi vs The State Food Insepctor on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193811281/ 2 Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
